newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end lower in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end lower in all months.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures closed lower across the board on Tuesday as lower bullion prices accelerated selling by local investors, traders said.
Prices were three to 10 yen lower, with the benchmark June 1998 contract down four yen at 1,160 yen per gram.
Spot gold was quoted at $318.80/319.30 per ounce at 0713 GMT, against $319.70/20 in New York on Monday.

Light selling orders from local investors emerged from the opening, mainly due to the New York market's price falls overnight, traders said. The lower bullion prices accelerated selling in the afternoon, they said.
Platinum futures ended mixed. Prices ranged from 18 yen lower to six yen higher, with benchmark June down six yen at 1,307 yen per gram.
Technical selling capped the topside, following the price gains on Monday, traders said. "But the situation is unchanged. Physical supplies are tight," a brokerage house trader said.

Russia has resumed its PGM exports for this year, but persistent concerns over the stability of Russian supplies next year are seen as a bullish factor for the market. "We couldn't find clear direction today," another trader said.
Prices were four yen lower to four yen higher, with the benchmark June up two yen at 515 yen per gram.
Silver was lower in all months. Benchmark June was down 3.6 yen at 158.6 yen per 10 grams.
